rounds.proof_sketch: eps changes from 1e-5 to 1.01e-5 (1% increase). inv_std = 1/sqrt(var+eps). Maximum relative change in inv_std occurs when var→0: ratio = sqrt(1.01) ≈ 1.00498, giving ~0.5% relative error. Since rtol=1e-2 (1%) and the error is always ≤0.5%, the condition |diff| > atol + rtol*|ref| is never satisfiable.
rounds.survival_reason: The epsilon perturbation from 1e-5 to 1.01e-5 creates at most a 0.5% relative difference in the inverse standard deviation term, which propagates linearly to the output. The torch.allclose tolerance with rtol=1e-2 allows 1% relative error. Since 0.5% < 1%, no input values can produce a difference exceeding the tolerance threshold. The absolute tolerance (atol=1e-2) also cannot be exceeded because when variance approaches zero (maximizing epsilon's influence), the normalized outputs also approach zero.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable. The 1% epsilon perturbation produces at most 0.5% output deviation, which is strictly within the 1% relative tolerance. Mathematical analysis shows the inequality |diff| > 0.01 + 0.01*|ref| cannot be satisfied for any input configuration.
rounds.recommendations: When testing epsilon perturbations in normalization kernels, use tighter tolerances (e.g., rtol=1e-4) to catch small stability-related mutations. The current 1% tolerance masks mutations that change numerical constants by up to ~2%.
